title: Warehouse Robot Inventory Management
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D warehouse robot inventory management simulation using Three.js (CDN). The scene simulates a top-down warehouse floor where an autonomous robot picks up crates from shelves and delivers them to a dispatch zone.

## Scene Setup
- Camera: Orthographic or perspective camera positioned above and angled (isometric-like view) looking down at the warehouse floor. The floor is a 20x20 unit grid.
- Lighting: Ambient light (0x404040) + one directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) from above-right.
- Floor: A flat plane with a subtle grid texture or wireframe overlay so grid cells are visible.
- Shelves: Place 3 shelf units (colored boxes, e.g. brown/tan) at fixed grid positions: Shelf A at (−6, 0.5, −6), Shelf B at (0, 0.5, −6), Shelf C at (6, 0.5, −6). Each shelf starts with 4 crates stacked visually.
- Crates: Small colored boxes (0.6 unit cubes). Each crate has a unique ID (C1–C12). Shelf A has C1–C4 (red), Shelf B has C5–C8 (green), Shelf C has C9–C12 (blue).
- Robot: A small box (0.8x0.4x0.8) colored yellow with a small sphere on top (antenna), starting at position (0, 0.2, 6). The robot moves on the XZ plane at Y=0.2.
- Dispatch Zone: A marked rectangular area at (0, 0.01, 8) shown as a glowing or highlighted green rectangle (3x3 units).

## Robot Movement & Physics
- The robot moves in a grid-aligned fashion. Each move step is 1 unit. Movement is animated (lerp over 300ms).
- Arrow keys (or WASD) move the robot: Up/W = -Z, Down/S = +Z, Left/A = -X, Right/D = +X.
- The robot cannot move outside the floor bounds (−10 to 10 on X and Z).
- Movement speed: track total distance traveled by the robot in units.

## Inventory Interactions
- When the robot is adjacent to a shelf (within 1.5 units) and the user presses 'E', the robot picks up the top crate from that shelf. The crate disappears from the shelf and visually attaches on top of the robot.
- The robot can carry at most 2 crates at a time (stacked on top).
- When the robot is inside the dispatch zone and the user presses 'Q', all carried crates are deposited. They appear stacked in the dispatch zone and are counted as dispatched.
- Each pickup and deposit is logged with a timestamp.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left HUD panel (HTML overlay) showing:
  - Robot position: 'Pos: (x, z)'
  - Carried crates: list of crate IDs currently held
  - Total dispatched count
  - Total distance traveled (integer units)
- A 'Reset' button that resets the entire simulation to initial state.
- A 'Auto-Run' button that commands the robot to automatically go to Shelf A, pick up 2 crates, deliver to dispatch, then go to Shelf B, pick up 2, deliver, cycling through all shelves. The auto-run should be stoppable by pressing the button again.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- robotPosition: {x, z} — current grid-aligned position
- robotCarrying: [] — array of crate ID strings currently carried
- shelfInventory: {A: [...], B: [...], C: [...]} — arrays of crate IDs remaining on each shelf
- dispatchedCrates: [] — array of crate IDs successfully dispatched
- totalDispatched: number
- totalDistance: number — total units the robot has moved
- isAutoRunning: boolean
- robotMoving: boolean — true while robot is mid-animation
- maxCarry: 2
- simTime: number — elapsed seconds since page load
- lastAction: string — last action performed e.g. 'pickup_C1', 'deposit', 'move_left', 'reset'
- canPickup: boolean — true if robot is adjacent to a shelf with crates
- canDeposit: boolean — true if robot is in dispatch zone with crates
physics_constraints: Robot must stay within floor bounds (−10 to 10 on X and Z). Robot cannot carry more than 2 crates. Crate counts must be conserved: shelfInventory totals + robotCarrying.length + dispatchedCrates.length must always equal 12. Movement is grid-aligned (integer positions). Distance increments by exactly 1 per move step.
